idiom_name: Akka typed FSM (one Behavior per state) or Play ActionBuilder composition
implementation_notes: On the JVM the pattern is library-provided in two shapes: an Akka actor whose behaviours are the flow states - each state is a Behaviors.receiveMessage handler returning the next behaviour, with the step's data carried by the enclosing method's parameters and timers handling step timeouts or expiry - or a Play action pipeline where ActionBuilder/ActionFunction values compose the per-step checks and the route file only points at the already-composed action. Both replace the classic command-object registry: commands become message types handled per behaviour or request types handled per composed action, and the view is what the behaviour/action finally returns. Choose the actor form when the flow must be persistent and distributed (persist the state, or use Akka Persistence) and the action-composition form when the flow is request-scoped and short.
pitfalls: A behaviour that closes over mutable state breaks the actor model; carry the data in the returned behaviour (as above) or in Behaviors.setup-built state, never in a var.
Messages a behaviour does not handle are silently unhandled; add an explicit catch-all that logs, otherwise a misspelled event leaves the flow stuck with no trace.
Play action composition is ordered: a builder that consumes the request body before your step guard runs leaves the guard validating an empty request, so the guard must come first.
